checks.claim: Older Cessna 172s, such as the 172R, have a maximum takeoff weight of about 2,450 lb (1,111 kg); newer 172S models are certified to 2,550 lb (1,157 kg).
checks.why: The FAA data sheet summary lists 2,450 lb for the 172R, and the 1,111 kg conversion is correct. The 172S/SP is higher at 2,550 lb (1,157 kg), and earlier models are lower. So the figure is not true for every 172 and needs the model qualifier.

checks.claim: A Cessna 172 rotates at about 55 knots indicated airspeed, roughly 100 km/h.
checks.why: Flying magazine, citing the POH, and the Purdue 172SP data sheet both give 55 KIAS as the rotation speed. 55 kt is about 102 km/h. It is the speed at which the pilot raises the nose, not a groundspeed, so it is worded as rotation at indicated airspeed.
